rationale: Seeds [] -> 0 impacted modules via the reverse import graph; routes from none; migrations_needed=False; blast radius 0.0.
alternatives_considered: grep-based impact estimate (cheaper, misses transitive importers)
outcome: Empty workspace: greenfield build, no existing code is impacted.

rationale: Capabilities ['core'] decomposed from the catalog. Independent work runs in parallel (implement.codes, implement.foundation, implement.urls); tests and docs branch after implementation and join at review; release waits for review.
alternatives_considered: Single sequential pipeline: simpler, but slower and one failure stalls everything
One mega implement node: fewer gates, far larger blast radius per failure

rationale: 302 by default (307 configurable): 301 is cached forever by browsers, breaking disable/delete and analytics; 7-char random base62 codes with bounded retry: 62^7 = 3.5e12; per-insert collision p = n/62^7; no central counter to coordinate; Soft delete + 410 Gone: keeps audit history and prevents silent alias re-use; Idempotency-Key stored on the link with a request fingerprint: simple, transactional, survives restarts

Everything the feature nodes share is built first so they can proceed in parallel: pydantic-settings config (12-factor, SHORTENER_ prefix), SQLAlchemy 2.0 async engine with a UTC-safe datetime type, Alembic migration 0001 (links table, unique code + idempotency key), JSON logging with request ids, a single error envelope, pure-ASGI middleware (request id, security headers, body size limit) and liveness/readiness probes. Test fixtures migrate a template DB once and copy it per test.
alternatives_considered: Base.metadata.create_all instead of Alembic: rejected, schema history and reversible migrations are required
BaseHTTPMiddleware: rejected, pure ASGI avoids its known streaming/background-task pitfalls
outcome: Service foundation - settings, async DB layer, initial migration, logging, errors, middleware, health probes

rationale: 7 random base62 characters give 62^7 = 3.5e12 codes; per-insert collision probability is n/62^7, so a bounded retry (5) plus the DB unique constraint is sufficient and avoids a central counter. Aliases are validated by regex (3-32 chars) and checked against reserved route names.
alternatives_considered: Sequential ids encoded in base62: rejected, enumerable and leaks volume
Hash of the URL: rejected, same URL from different users would collide by design
outcome: Base62 short-code generation (CSPRNG) and custom-alias validation with reserved words

rationale: Shorteners are abused for phishing and SSRF-style probing. Only http/https are accepted, embedded credentials are rejected, private/loopback/link-local IP literals and local host names are refused by default (configurable), and the URL is normalised so equivalent inputs store identically.
alternatives_considered: Resolve DNS to block private targets: deferred, adds latency and is racy (DNS rebinding); documented
outcome: Target URL validation and normalisation (http/https only, no private hosts, no credentials)

rationale: LinkService holds the use cases; the repository isolates SQL. Create supports Idempotency-Key with a request fingerprint (replay returns the original link, misuse returns 409). Redirect returns 302 by default (307 configurable) with Cache-Control no-store so every click reaches the service. Custom aliases are stored in canonical lower case and alias conflicts are checked case-insensitively. NOTE (deliberate, documented): lookups use exact matching, so an alias created as 'MyLink' is not reachable at /MyLink. This is the seeded defect fixed by the brownfield scenario.
alternatives_considered: 301 redirects: rejected, browsers cache them permanently which breaks disable/delete and analytics
outcome: Links API - create (idempotent), metadata, patch, soft delete, and the public redirect

rationale: Hypothesis explores input spaces that example tests miss (unicode, huge integers, odd schemes).
alternatives_considered: Only example-based tests: rejected, weaker guarantees for parsers/encoders
outcome: Property-based tests for base62 round-trips, ordering, URL normalisation idempotence and scheme safety

rationale: Exercises the API end-to-end against a real migrated SQLite database, including the concurrency and retry paths that unit tests cannot reach, and proves migrations upgrade/downgrade cleanly.
alternatives_considered: Mocks for the database: rejected, would not catch constraint/race behaviour
outcome: Integration tests - lifecycle, case-sensitive generated codes, collision retry, concurrency, idempotency races, migrations
